newsitem.title: USA: UBS trims Peru, Colombia portfolio allocations.
newsitem.headline: UBS trims Peru, Colombia portfolio allocations.

text.p: UBS Securities said it cut its asset allocations on Peru and Colombia to underweight and market weight, respectively, in a reshuffling of its Latin American equities portfolio.
The firm said in a statement released Tuesday that it reduced Peru's weighting to three percent from 3.2 percent and cut Colombia's allocation to 2.5 percent from 4.2 percent.

Peru's "recent economic rebound owes to natural resources," the statement said. The rest of the economy is stagnating because of a tight fiscal and monetary policy to which Peru will adhere through commitments to the International Monetary Fund.
The firm recommended stocks of banks, such as Banco Wiese Ltdo and telecommunications companies, such as Telefonica del Peru SA.
On Colombia, UBS said the political crisis had taken its toll on economic growth. The banking and construction and cement sectors appear poised for a rebound next year.
The firm said it maintained Chile's underweight allocation at 10 percent, but trimmed Argentina's overweight position to 12 percent from 13 percent.
